preamble.summary:
The second plan of the spec `command-contracts`. Plan 1 (`command-runner-and-mod-answers`, PR #184) ported the command library to Effect 3, put the bridge between Commander and the runner, and moved `ls`, `artifact status`, `plans lint` and `plans overview`. This plan moves the inspection commands onto the runner through that bridge, each with its output contract, its render (today's text), its declared errors with today's sentences and codes, and its help, examples and completer moved into its definition: `validate`, `session-info`, `path`, `brief`, `architecture`, `completions` and `report`; the groups `cost`, `schema`, `security`, `skills` and `records`, each moved whole; and the rest of `plans` (`status`, `overlap`, `estimate`), after which `plans` too is a group the runner holds whole. `artifact` stays bridged until plan 3.

Phases: phase-01 gives the port and the bridge what these commands need (a group's long help and examples, variadic arguments, negated switches, a command that prompts refusing `--json`, groups held whole by the runner) and one contract test over every runner command. phase-02 moves the rest of `plans`. phase-03 moves the seven root inspection commands. phase-04 moves `cost`, `schema`, `security` and `skills`. phase-05 writes the acceptance tests of `records`, and phase-06 moves `records` and passes them.

Criteria this plan advances on the commands it moves, still finished by plans 3 and 4 (they hold for the whole program only once the last command moves):
- ac-json-every-command, ac-text-unchanged, ac-error-sentence, ac-unknown-option, ac-help and ac-no-parser: every moved command.
- ac-catalogue: one entry per moved command.
- ac-groups: `plans`, `cost`, `schema`, `security`, `skills` and `records` alone; `artifact`, `artifact new` and `agent setup` wait for plan 3.
- ac-written: `skills install`, `schema upgrade`, `cost backfill`, `records init` and `plans status --apply`; `artifact approve` waits for plan 3.
- ac-no-person: `records init`; `enter` and `artifact decide` wait for plans 3 and 4.
- ac-usage-parity: the moved commands' blocks come from their definitions; the file is the generator's output from the definitions alone only after plan 4.

Criteria this plan does not touch: ac-stdin-file-or-dash, ac-stdin-terminal, ac-stdin-bad, ac-brief-text and ac-written-on-failure's command case (plan 3, `artifact decide` and `artifact new`), ac-progress and ac-error-sentence's `resume` case (plan 4), and ac-versioned-stable (no versioned document changes here). No criterion is finished in full by this plan.

Execution caveat: this repository is driven by the installed phax during the run, and nothing this plan changes is read by it. Every test proves the runner through its `Io` data, through a kept run function, or through `tsx src/cli/main.ts` spawned in a temporary repository (tests/helpers/isolateGit.ts, a temporary PHAX home). No test reads ~/.phax, a real ~/.claude, ~/.codex or ~/.vibe, the global git config or the real `gh`, runs a real provider or a real Claude Code probe, or holds a fact the release cut changes (a snapshot named `next`, the version in package.json).
preamble.requiredCommandsNote: Both commands are already in `security.agentCommands` in phax.json: `pnpm gen:usage-spec` rewrites phax.usage.kdl and `pnpm docs:cli` rewrites the README's generated CLI block. No security configuration change is needed. The plan declares no skill file, so the run needs no `--allow-skill-edits`.
technicalArbitrations: Output contracts. The spec creates no format beyond plan 1's four (§6 `package`), so every output in this plan carries no `$schema`, as §6's `unlock --json` shows. `plans status`, `plans overlap` and `plans estimate` keep today's unversioned `--json` object as their output contract byte for byte: same keys, same order, same values, two-space indent and one trailing newline, the output schema written so that encoding today's value gives exactly `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)`. The one change is `plans status --apply`, whose object (it already differs from the plain one by `applied`) gains `written` after `applied`: the flipped plans' written-file records (§5.18). Loss accepted: a reader gets no `$schema` to validate these objects by URL, only the contract `--json-schema` prints, and a later change of their shape is announced by no stamp. Changing them (a `$schema`, renamed keys) would abandon §6's package surface and every script reading today's object.

Commands whose text is a script's input answer an object under `--json`, never a document through the `document` hook, because a document's bytes under `--json` would not parse as JSON (ac-json-every-command). `path` answers `{ qualifiedName, crossProject, worktreePath }`; its render prints `Target: <qualified name>` then the path when the run is another project's, else the path alone, so `cd "$(phax path …)"` reads today's bytes. `completions <shell>` answers `{ shell, script }`; its render is the script with one trailing newline removed (the runner adds one back). `records explain` answers the explained record with the text of each artifact a flag asks for (`--prompt`, `--diff`, `--transcript`, `--gates`, `--briefs`), decoded as the text print decodes it today. Without `--json` each prints today's bytes. Loss accepted: a completion script `usage` printed without a final newline gains one.

Written files. A command reports as written-file records (the port's `Written`, src/cli/commandLibrary/contract/written.ts) the files that are its deliverable: `skills install` each file it installs (none for a skill already present), `schema upgrade` phax.schema.json and the user schema when it updates them, `cost backfill` each cost-ledger.json it writes, `records init` the phax.json it configures, `plans status --apply` each flipped plan. Each digest is computed from the bytes read back after the write. A file inside the repository has its path from the repository root; a file outside it (~/.phax, ~/.claude) has its absolute path, since there is no repository root for it. None of them answers a document, so none takes `--out`: `--out` is for an answer that is one document, and each of these answers a report with several records or none. `records sync` writes into a Git clone, not a file the caller reads by path: it answers today's sync result (what it pulled, pushed or found pending) with no written-file record. Phax's own side state is not reported: `plans estimate`'s backfilled ledgers stay the stderr line they are today, `plans overlap`'s extraction cache, the registry, locks, `brief`'s brief-NN.json records and `report`'s temporary files. Loss accepted: §5.18 is read as a command's deliverables, so a reader of `plans estimate --json` learns of the ledgers it wrote only from a note line.

Providers, network and persons. No moved command gains a progress line a person does not read today (§5.4): `brief` and `architecture` ask their provider and print nothing before the answer; `plans estimate`'s Claude Code probe and `plans overlap`'s extraction on a cache miss print nothing while they run; `report` prints only `Issue created: <url>` after its `gh` calls. What they print on stderr today becomes `progress` when it is printed as it happens (`plans estimate`'s `Wrote N cost ledgers …` line, printed after the backfill and before the report) and `notes` when it is derived from the output (`plans estimate`'s `Warning: …` lines, `plans status`'s orphan-record warnings, `brief`'s record warning). Under `--json` both are note lines. None of these commands waits on a person, so none refuses `--json`, except `records init`, which prompts through its Prompt port on every call: it declares that it prompts, and `--json` is refused before anything starts (§5.20). Under `--json`, `--json` alone never makes a command prompt.

Where the definitions live: one file per command or per group under src/cli/definitions/, as plan 1's are: plansStatus.ts, plansOverlap.ts, plansEstimate.ts, validate.ts, sessionInfo.ts, path.ts, brief.ts, architecture.ts, completions.ts, report.ts, and cost.ts, schema.ts, security.ts, skills.ts and records.ts (with recordsExplain.ts for explain's renders) each holding a group and its commands. A moved command's Commander registration is deleted from src/cli/program.ts or its register function, and its entry in src/cli/cliDocs.ts is deleted, not kept beside its definition. Its file under src/cli/commands/ is deleted, or kept only as the run function an existing test imports (runValidate, runBrief, runArchitecture, runCostBackfill, runSchemaUpgrade, runSkillsInstall, runPlansStatus, runPlansOverlap, runPlansEstimate), each a composition of its definition through `runThroughOutput` (src/cli/bridge.ts), as plan 1 kept runLs. src/cli/cliCompleters.ts keeps its `short-name` entry, which unmigrated commands (resume, enter, run, …) still declare until plan 4; a moved command declares the same completer on its argument's annotation, and the generator writes one `complete "short-name"` node, never two.

The bridge after this plan. Its routing holds one constant, the groups the runner holds in part: `artifact` alone (phase-01 starts it as `artifact` and `plans`, phase-02 removes `plans`). Every other runner group is held whole: a call naming it, alone, with `--help`, through `help <group>`, or with a word that names none of its commands, goes to the runner, which writes its help and refuses with 64. A call naming a runner command goes to the runner as today. Everything else goes to Commander: root help, `--version`, the `artifact` group and every unmigrated command stay Commander's until plan 4. A whole group is mounted in the Commander tree as a help-only group stub, registered like a command stub, so root help lists it at its place and the generator splices the runner's whole group block there. Loss accepted: until plan 4 a whole group's block in phax.usage.kdl gains `subcommand_required=#true`, which the frozen-file test allows per whole group.

Gains and one fix the port takes in phase-01, beyond §10's list, each written as the library would carry it with a doc comment and a conformance case, because without them these commands cannot keep their declarations (§5.21, §7): a group carries `help` and `examples`, shown in its help and written as its `long_help` and `example` nodes (`cost` and `plans` have long help today); a tuple's rest element is a variadic argument (`brief [path...]`, `architecture [path...]`, `plans overlap <plan...>`), written `[path]...` or `<plan>...` as today; a command declares `prompts`, a predicate over its decoded input, and the runner refuses `--json` before `run` when it holds (`records init` here, `artifact decide` without `--verdicts` and `enter` in later plans). The fix: a field such as `noProbe` is the switch `--no-probe`, and the Commander adapter reads Commander's negated attribute for it, which it misses today (`--no-probe`, `--no-extract`, `--no-gist`). Loss accepted: four more items for the published package to take upstream.

Inputs a command refuses itself stay strings. Where today's command answers a bad value with its own code and sentence (`completions` an unknown shell with exit 1, `skills install` an invalid `--target`, `--scope` or skill name with exit 2), the input contract declares a string, not a literal union, and `run` refuses with a declared error carrying today's sentence and code. Loss accepted: these values show no `choices` in help, the catalogue or phax.usage.kdl, as today, and a refused value is an `error` line rather than a `refused` line under `--json`.

Archived runs. A command reading a run does on an archived one what it does today. `session-info` and `path` resolve through resolveRunRef, which reads the run folder under runs/: an archived run is refused with today's `is in the registry but its files could not be read` sentence and exit 1. `report <run>` reads runs/<short-name>/semantic.jsonl and fails with today's `phax report failed: …` sentence and exit 1 when the run is archived. `cost backfill` reads the archived run folder (<archivePath>/runs) as it does today. `records` reads records on phax/records/v1 and the registry, not run folders, and is unchanged for an archived run. `plans overlap --landed` reads the landed run's global-file-reconciliation.json where it does today.

Tests. phase-01 writes one in-phase contract test over every command and whole group of `phaxProgram`, through the runner's memory Io: `--json-schema` equals the catalogue entry and runs nothing, `--help` lists `--json`, an undeclared option is refused with 64 (a `refused` line from `flags` under `--json`), and a whole group alone writes its help and is refused. It never runs a command, so each later phase's commands are covered by it as they join the program. Each family adds its own `--json`, error-sentence and written-file tests in the phase that moves it; only `records`, the largest family and the one with a prompting command, gets an acceptance pair. Every acceptance test carries its own `.fails` marker on its own `it`, fails on its own assertion, and is changed by the passing phase only by removing that marker. Loss accepted: the other families' tests are written with the code, not frozen before it.

Existing tests. They keep passing with their assertions unchanged. A test whose harness builds a Commander registration this plan deletes (tests/unit/skillsArgv.test.ts, tests/integration/recordsExplain.test.ts, tests/integration/recordsExplainStop.test.ts) has its harness replaced by the runner's, over a memory Io or `runThroughOutput`, and its assertions kept; an assertion that Commander's parse throws becomes the runner's refusal with 64. Registration checks of the moved commands in tests/integration/cliProgram.test.ts follow the stubs, as plan 1 did. Every such change is named in the phase's handoff.

Long help. Every moved command and group keeps its long help, examples, help and argument and option help word for word; this plan rewords none, so the frozen-file test's `REWORDED_LONG_HELP` list does not grow. Its allowlist grows only by `--json` on each moved command (reworded where the command declared its own: `plans status`, `plans overlap`, `plans estimate`), `subcommand_required` on each whole group, and what q-security-bare decides for `security`.

openQuestions.question: Today a bare `phax security` runs the status report and exits 0, and `security` and `security status` each declare their own `--verbose` and `--trace` in phax.usage.kdl. When the `security` group moves onto the runner whole (phase-04), what do they become?

options.label: Bare `phax security` writes its help on stderr and exits 64 like every group (§5.11); `--verbose` and `--trace` there are the program's options, and the frozen-file test allows dropping the group's and `security status`'s own declarations of them
options.abandons: the bare `phax security` shortcut (exit 0 with the report) and four flag declarations in phax.usage.kdl, a change §5.21 and §7 otherwise forbid

options.label: A further gain: a group may name a command it runs when called alone, and `security` runs `status`; the local `--verbose` and `--trace` declarations still go, read as program options
options.abandons: §5.11's rule that a group called alone is refused, for one group, and one more gain outside §10's list for the published package to take upstream

options.label: `security status` moves; the `security` group stays Commander's, with its bare action and its flags, until plan 4
options.abandons: ac-groups for `security` in this plan, and plan 4 inherits the same choice with the group's refusal still bridge glue

openQuestions.rationale: Every document and test names `phax security status`; the bare form appears only as `<SUBCOMMAND>` in the generated usage line, which already says a subcommand is expected. §5.11 is the spec's rule, the flags keep working anywhere in the call as program options, and the other two options either widen the contract for one shortcut or postpone the same decision.

phases.title: Runner groundwork: group help, variadic arguments, negated switches, prompting commands and whole groups
phases.objective: The port and the bridge can carry every inspection command without changing what it declares: a group has long help and examples, an argument can be variadic, a `--no-x` switch reaches its command, a command that prompts refuses `--json`, and a group the runner holds whole is routed, helped and refused by the runner. One contract test checks every runner command and whole group, so each command joins it as it moves.
detailedInstructions: Read this plan's Technical arbitrations (gains, the bridge, tests), src/cli/commandLibrary/contract/{command,define,shapes,usage,catalogue,index}.ts, src/cli/commandLibrary/commander/{commanderAdapter,run}.ts, contract/conformance/cases.ts and its suite, tests/unit/commandLibrary/conformance.test.ts (its CONTRACT_ONLY list), src/cli/bridge.ts and tests/unit/cli/bridge.test.ts, src/cli/program.ts, scripts/generate-usage-spec.ts, tests/integration/usageSpecDeclarations.test.ts and tests/helpers/usageKdl.ts. Check every Effect API against the installed `effect` in node_modules.

Gain, group help: `defineGroup` and `Grouping` take optional `help` and `examples`. The runner writes a group's help like a command's: its summary, then the long help, then `Examples:` with each example indented two spaces, then its commands. `usageSpec` writes them as the group's `long_help` and `example` nodes, in that order before its commands. Add the conformance case `groups.long-help`.

Gain, variadic arguments: a tuple contract's rest element is a variadic argument. `ArgShape` gains `variadic: boolean`; a rest element after required elements is required (`<plan...>`), a rest alone optional (`[path...]`). The Commander adapter declares `<name...>` or `[name...]` and hands every operand to the tuple. `usageSpec` writes it as today's generator does, `arg "<plan>..."` or `arg "[path]..."` with its help. Add the conformance case `args.variadic`.

Fix, negated switches: a Boolean field whose option starts with `no-` (field `noProbe`, option `--no-probe`) is declared to Commander as `--no-probe`, and the adapter reads Commander's attribute for it (`probe === false`), handing `noProbe: true` to `run` when it is given and leaving it absent otherwise. Help, catalogue and usage spec show `--no-probe` as today. Add the conformance case `flags.negated-switch`, and a runner test beside tests/unit/commandLibrary/commander/policies.test.ts.

Gain, prompting commands: `CommandDef.prompts?: (input) => boolean`, over the decoded input. When it holds and `--json` is given, the runner refuses the call after decoding and before `run`, with the program's `refused` code: one `refused` line with `source` "flags", `path` ["json"], `expected` "a call that does not prompt" and today's style of text (`error: --json: <command> prompts; run it without --json`). Without `--json` nothing changes. Add the conformance case `json.prompting-refused`. Each new case lists in CONTRACT_ONLY of tests/unit/commandLibrary/conformance.test.ts only if it holds without a runner.

Whole groups in src/cli/bridge.ts: add the constant of groups the runner holds in part, `PARTIAL_GROUPS = ["artifact", "plans"]`, with a comment that phase-02 removes `plans` and plan 3 empties it. `route` sends to the runner a call whose leading words, after program options, name a runner group not in that constant, whatever follows (alone, `--help`, an unknown word); `dispatch`'s `help <words>` path does the same. Add `mountRunnerGroupStub(parent, program, words)`: a help-only Commander group with the group's summary, holding a help-only stub of each of its commands, all registered in the stub registry; `mountRunnerStubs` skips the commands of a mounted group. `runnerUsage` also keys each whole group's full block (header with `subcommand_required=#true` and its commands) by its full name.

scripts/generate-usage-spec.ts: at a group stub, splice the runner's whole group block, indented to its depth. Keep writing one `complete` node per identifier: the union of src/cli/cliCompleters.ts and the completers the runner's arguments declare, cliCompleters first, never one identifier twice.

tests/integration/usageSpecDeclarations.test.ts: derive from `phaxProgram` and the bridge's PARTIAL_GROUPS the groups held whole, and allow each one's `subcommand_required` declaration (no group is held whole yet, so nothing is allowed yet). Keep `MIGRATED_COMMANDS` and the other lists as they are. Run `pnpm gen:usage-spec`: phax.usage.kdl must not change in this phase.

Write tests/unit/cli/runnerCommandContracts.test.ts, which never runs a command. For every command of `phaxProgram`, through `runner.run(phaxProgram, io)` with the memory Io of tests/unit/commandLibrary/commander/support/memoryIo.ts: `<words> --json-schema` prints one JSON value equal to that command's entry in `phax --json-schema` and exits 0; `<words> --help` exits 0 and its text lists `--json`; `<words> --colour --json` writes nothing on stdout, one `refused` line with `"source":"flags"` on stderr and exits 64; `<words> --colour` exits 64 with stderr starting `error: unknown option '--colour'`. For every group of `phaxProgram` not in PARTIAL_GROUPS, the group alone writes its help on stderr and exits 64. The catalogue holds exactly one entry per command of `phaxProgram`. A command whose argument is required gets placeholder values for the `--colour` cases, so the refusal is the option's.

tests/unit/cli/bridge.test.ts: `route` sends a whole group's calls (alone, `--help`, `help <group>`, an unknown word) to the runner and a partial group's to Commander; the group stub is registered. Extend tests/unit/commandLibrary/commander/groups.test.ts and usage.test.ts for the group help and the variadic argument where the runner's own tests group them.
phases.boundaryContracts: Producer: the port's contract (src/cli/commandLibrary/contract/index.ts). Consumers: phases 02 to 06's definitions. Contract: `defineGroup({ name, summary, help?, examples?, commands })`, a tuple rest element as a variadic argument, a `noX` Boolean field as the `--no-x` switch, and `prompts(input)` refusing `--json`. Producer: src/cli/bridge.ts (`PARTIAL_GROUPS`, `route`, `mountRunnerGroupStub`, `runnerUsage`). Consumers: src/cli/program.ts and scripts/generate-usage-spec.ts. Contract: a group outside PARTIAL_GROUPS is the runner's whole, mounted as a help-only group stub whose usage block is the runner's.

Describe how the adapter reads a negated switch. Give `PARTIAL_GROUPS`, `route`'s rule for whole groups, `mountRunnerGroupStub`'s signature, how `runnerUsage` keys a group block, and how the generator writes complete nodes from the union. commit.subject: feat(cli): group help, variadic arguments, negated switches and whole groups on the runner
commit.body:
Give the ported command library what the inspection commands need to keep their
declarations: a group's long help and examples, variadic arguments, `--no-x`
switches read from Commander's negated attribute, and a command that prompts
refusing `--json` before it runs. Each is a conformance case.

The bridge can hand a whole group to the runner, which then owns its help and its
refusal when called alone, and the usage spec generator splices the group's block.
One contract test checks every runner command's `--json-schema`, `--help` and
unknown-option refusal, and every whole group called alone.

phases.assignmentReason: The phase designs four contract shapes the port does not hold and changes the bridge's routing for whole groups, across the contract, the Commander adapter, the bridge and the usage generator.

phases.title: plans status, overlap and estimate on the runner, plans held whole
phases.objective: `phax plans status`, `phax plans overlap` and `phax plans estimate` are command definitions on the runner, and the runner holds the `plans` group whole. Their `--json` objects are today's bytes, their text, warnings, sentences and codes are today's, and `phax plans` alone is the runner's help and refusal.
detailedInstructions: Read this plan's Technical arbitrations (output contracts, written files, providers, definitions, the bridge, tests, existing tests), src/cli/definitions/{program,plansLint,plansOverview,shared}.ts, src/cli/bridge.ts (`runThroughOutput`, PARTIAL_GROUPS, `mountRunnerGroupStub`), src/cli/commands/{plans,plansOverlap,plansEstimate}.ts, src/cli/cliDocs.ts (`plans`, `plans status`, `plans overlap`, `plans estimate`), src/app/planStaleness.ts, src/app/analyzePlanOverlap.ts, src/app/estimatePlan.ts and the tests of the three commands.

Before changing a command, write the oracle of byte-for-byte JSON: tests/unit/cli/plansInspectionContracts.test.ts encodes, through each new output contract, fixed values of today's shapes (a staleness report with orphan records, with and without `applied`; an overlap result and a readjustment impact; an estimate report for each verdict kind) and expects exactly `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)` plus one newline, the bytes today's command prints. Values come from the domain types, written by hand in the test.

src/cli/definitions/plansStatus.ts: flags `apply` ("Flip stale-computed plans Approved -> Stale"); output today's object, `{ report, orphanRecords }`, or with `--apply` `{ report, orphanRecords, applied, written }`, `written` the flipped plans' written-file records (repo-relative, digest of the bytes read back). Render today's report, then a blank line and the apply text under `--apply`. Notes: one orphan-record warning per orphan, as renderOrphanRecordWarning words it. Errors: a config error exits 1 with `Config error: …`, others with exitCodeForError's code and their message.

src/cli/definitions/plansOverlap.ts: args `<plan...>` (variadic, "Paths to two or more plan.md files"); flags `noExtract` (`--no-extract`) and `landed`. Output today's `resultToJson` object, or `impactToJson`'s with `--landed`. Render today's text. Errors exit 1 with today's sentences (`Config error: …` for the config). The extraction on a cache miss writes no progress line.

src/cli/definitions/plansEstimate.ts: args `<plan>`, flag `noProbe` (`--no-probe`). Output today's report as is. The `Wrote N cost ledger(s) for kept runs that had none.` line is a `progress` call made after the backfill, worded as today; each `report.warnings` entry is a note `Warning: <warning>`. Render as today, with the local time zone and the clock. Errors keep exitCodeForError's codes (1, 2, 10, 12) and `Config error: …` with 1. Tests use `--no-probe` or the fake provider backend, never a real probe.

Each definition moves its help and examples word for word from cliDocs, and its argument and option help from today's registration, and declares `--json`'s meaning through the runner only. Provide each run's layers inside it, from src/cli/commands/runLayers.ts, as plan 1's definitions do.

Delete the four cliDocs entries.

commit.subject: feat(cli): the records group answers through the command runner
commit.body:
Write records init, sync, status, list and explain as command definitions, and let
the runner hold the records group whole. `--json` answers one value per command,
explain carrying the text of the artifacts its flags ask for; `records init`
prompts, so `--json` is refused before it starts, and it answers phax.json's
written-file record.

Without `--json` every records command prints today's text and error sentences with
today's codes. The group's acceptance tests pass with their markers removed.

phases.assignmentReason: A passing phase whose acceptance tests are frozen, over explain's eight outcome kinds whose text must stay byte for byte: higher effort, so the phase does not stop on a disagreement it could have avoided.
